clue.text: Bowler's second stopping run … leads economically to 3 down

definitions.note: a cryptic description of the feat: three batsmen out in three balls

parts.note: a bowler is a hard round felt hat

indicators.note: to stop something is to plug it, so one piece sits inside the other as a stopper

parts.note: a tick is a moment, as in 'just a tick'
R is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A cricket commentator describes a bowler cutting off runs and ripping through the batting with a sequence of quick wickets.
explanation.walkthrough: '3 down' looks like a cross-reference to 3 down (ROLE MODEL), but here it simply means three wickets fallen. HAT + T(R)ICK = HAT-TRICK.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a bowler takes this by dismissing three batsmen with consecutive deliveries, the most efficient possible way of getting three wickets.

clue.text: Witches, soldier included in something distinctly Scottish

indicators.note: to be included in something is to be placed inside it

parts.note: hags are witches
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: Witches and a soldier are bundled into a scene of quintessential Scottishness, like a Macbeth staging.
explanation.definitionFit: Haggis, a savoury pudding of offal, oatmeal and spices cooked in a sheep's stomach, is Scotland's national dish.

clue.text: It's a complex container for rising Doctor!

definitions.text: It's a complex container for rising Doctor!

indicators.note: a container holds something, so one piece is wrapped round the others

parts.note: 'tis is the poetic contraction of it is
taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means read from the bottom up, so the abbreviation is turned around

parts.note: Dr is the standard abbreviation for doctor

explanation.surface: A sci-fi fan exclaims about the elaborate time machine the Doctor climbs into.
explanation.walkthrough: 'TIS holds A plus DR reversed (RD): T(ARD)IS. The whole clue also describes the answer: in Doctor Who, the Tardis is a complicated vessel that the Doctor travels in.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tardis is the time-travelling police box of the BBC series Doctor Who, famously far bigger inside than out.

clue.text: Not initially well groomed — could become one to emulate

indicators.note: could become suggests a transformation, so the remaining letters are turned into something new
not initially means without the opening, so each word here loses its first letter

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A scruffy person might yet turn into someone others look up to.
explanation.walkthrough: Both words lose their first letters, leaving ELL and ROOMED, which are rearranged into ROLE MODEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A role model is a person whose behaviour is admired and copied by others, someone held up as an example.

clue.text: Mathematician blathers madly, wasting time in Savoy

indicators.note: in places the jumbled letters inside the other word
wasting means throwing away, so the word sheds one of its letters

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
a Savoy is a variety of crinkly-leaved cabbage

indicators.note: madly suggests wild disorder, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A mathematician rambles wildly, frittering away hours at the Savoy hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Savoy' looks like the famous London hotel, but it is the crinkly-leaved vegetable variety, wrapped around the jumbled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Babbage was the Victorian polymath who designed the Difference Engine and Analytical Engine, early mechanical computers.

clue.text: Reconstituted spare parts for Everyman in the old country

indicators.note: something reconstituted has been broken down and put back together in a different form

parts.note: taken as written
the setter, Everyman, refers to himself as I

explanation.surface: Somebody has refurbished spare parts and sent them to the setter, who lives in some former homeland.
explanation.walkthrough: A setter's pseudonym in the clue stands for I or ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Persia was the historic name of the country now called Iran, used officially until 1935.

clue.text: Polish team regularly getting goal

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second and fourth letters
an end is an aim or goal, as in 'to that end'

explanation.surface: A national football side from Poland scores regularly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' with a capital looks like the nationality; it is the verb meaning refine.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend a text is to correct and improve it, to polish it by removing errors.

clue.text: Primarily, something hollered out with the utmost noisy energy?

definitions.text: something hollered out with the utmost noisy energy?

indicators.note: primarily means in the first place, so the opening letter of each word is taken

parts.words: something hollered out with the utmost noisy energy
parts.note: the initial letters of the eight words

explanation.surface: A description of belting out a big number at full volume.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as a description of the answer: a Broadway number is typically sung out loudly with maximum energy.
explanation.definitionFit: A show tune is a song from a stage musical, typically a big, rousing number belted out by the cast.

clue.text: Incorrectly, 'the May stone'; it's the February birthstone

indicators.note: incorrectly means the order given is wrong and must be put right

parts.note: taken as written
ST is the abbreviation for stone, the unit of weight

explanation.surface: A pedant corrects someone who called a gem May's stone, pointing out it belongs to February.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The May stone' reads as a mistaken claim about birthstones; it is fodder, with stone abbreviated.
explanation.definitionFit: Amethyst, a purple variety of quartz, is the traditional gem assigned to those born in February.

clue.text: Riotous pastoral events?

indicators.note: riotous means wild and disorderly, so the letters run amok

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Wild goings-on in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines the answer: the 1381 uprising was a riot of rural labourers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Peasants' Revolt of 1381 was a major English rebellion of rural workers led by Wat Tyler against the poll tax.

clue.text: Our cousin's a warrior, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is a word spoken out loud rather than read, so sound matters, not spelling

parts.note: a guerrilla is an irregular fighter, and the word is pronounced like the ape

explanation.surface: Someone boasts that a relative of theirs is a fearsome fighter.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorillas are great apes, among humanity's closest living relatives in evolutionary terms, hence a cousin of ours.

clue.text: You can see right through this earl with the old predicament

definitions.text: You can see right through this

parts.note: E is an abbreviation for earl
ye is the archaic form of the, as in 'Ye Olde Shoppe'
to be in a hole is to be in a predicament

explanation.surface: An aristocrat in an awkward fix is utterly transparent to everyone around him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See right through' sounds like seeing through someone's deceit, but here it is literal looking.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyehole is a small opening, as in a mask or door, that you put your eye to and look out through.

clue.text: Fool almost getting married, in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: almost means not quite all there, so the word falls short of its final letter

parts.note: an idiot is a fool
M is the abbreviation for married in genealogies and forms

explanation.surface: A not-quite-foolish person is, so to speak, getting married.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a manner of speaking' reads as a stock phrase meaning 'so to speak', hiding the definition inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom is an established expression or turn of phrase peculiar to a language, a characteristic way of saying something.

clue.text: In desperation, hold out scrap

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective, 'made in desperation', as in a last-ditch attempt

parts.note: to last is to hold out or endure
to ditch something is to scrap or discard it

explanation.surface: Someone desperately clings on to a small leftover fragment.
explanation.definitionFit: A last-ditch effort is a final, desperate attempt to avoid failure, from fighting at the last defensive trench.

clue.text: Advice lacking energy, odd: 'Stand one's ground'

indicators.note: ground in the sense of milled or crushed, so the letters are broken up and remixed
lacking means going without, so the following item is left out of the mix

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A rather odd piece of guidance, delivered without much energy: 'Stand one's ground'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stand one's ground' looks like a quoted motto, but 'ground' is the anagram signal. Remove the E from ODD STAND ONES and rearrange to get DOS AND DON'TS.
explanation.definitionFit: Dos and don'ts are rules of conduct listing what one should and should not do, a set of guidance or recommendations.

clue.text: Finding crater on island, attempt practice with canines

parts.note: a dent is a hollow, a small crater
IS is the abbreviation for island
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: A dog-training session finds a crater on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canines' suggests dogs, but here they are the pointed teeth beside the incisors.
explanation.definitionFit: Dentistry is the profession of caring for teeth, and canines are teeth, so a dental practice deals with them.

clue.text: Cold shaken off, biceps flexed, a doctor's inserted instrument

indicators.note: inserted means put inside, so these pieces go into the other word
a flexed muscle changes shape, so the letters are bent into a new order
something shaken off is got rid of, so that letter goes

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
taken as written
taken as written
a GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor

explanation.surface: After shaking off a chill and flexing their arms, a patient has a medical instrument inserted by the doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Instrument' fits the medical surface as a surgical tool, but it is a musical one; the doctor and the article go in after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Bagpipes are a wind instrument, played by squeezing air from a bag through reed pipes, closely associated with Scotland.

clue.text: Partridge perhaps pulls funny face earlier in absurd endeavour

indicators.note: earlier tells us which piece comes first when the two are put side by side

parts.note: to mug is to pull faces, especially for a camera
partridge is an example of game bird

explanation.surface: Alan Partridge, the TV comedy character, gurns his way through a ridiculous undertaking.
explanation.walkthrough: Partridge suggests the comedy character; it is just a game bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A mug's game is an activity only a fool would take on, because it is pointless or unprofitable.

clue.text: Southern guy is nasal, revolting, disgusting

indicators.note: revolting here means rising up in revolt, so the letters overthrow their order

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for southern
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man from the South talks through his nose and is described as utterly repulsive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolting' looks like a second insult in the list, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something extremely unpleasant or repellent to look at, an intensified way of calling it hideous.

clue.text: Pervert hides letter from Greece; it involves muscle-stretching

indicators.note: to hide something is to conceal it inside, so one piece is wrapped round another

parts.note: to warp is to pervert or distort
mu is the twelfth letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A deviant conceals a letter from Greece, in a story about gym exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: A warm-up is a session of light exercise and stretching done to prepare the body before strenuous activity.

clue.text: Knight abandons aggressive tone

indicators.note: to abandon is to leave behind, so that letter drops out

parts.note: violent means aggressive
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A chivalrous knight drops his hostile manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tone' sounds like a manner of speaking, but here it is a shade of colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Violet is a bluish-purple shade, a hue or tint, which is a sense of the word tone.

clue.text: Errant — so bad — pole dance

indicators.note: errant means straying from the proper course, so the letters wander out of order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A judge pans someone's shambolic pole-dancing routine as wayward and dreadful.
explanation.definitionFit: The paso doble is a fast Latin ballroom routine modelled on the drama of a Spanish bullfight.

clue.text: Man fleeing bright-bottomed baboon? That's boring

definitions.note: noun sense: a drill is a tool that does the boring

indicators.note: fleeing means running away, so those letters leave the word

parts.note: the mandrill is a baboon-like monkey famous for its colourful face and rump
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone runs away from a colourful baboon, and a bystander shrugs that it is all rather dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' reads as dull, but it is the act of making holes. As a bonus the drill is also a baboon, a close relative of the mandrill.
explanation.definitionFit: A drill is a tool for making holes, and boring means cutting a hole through material, which is what a drill does.

clue.text: One in 5 now wanting some veterinarian to return

definitions.note: 5 across is PERSIA, the old name of Iran

indicators.note: returning means going back the way you came, so the letters are read backwards
some means only a portion, so the answer lies within the longer word

parts.note: the run of letters in the middle of the word

explanation.surface: Someone living in the region today wants a vet to come back.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference 5 is PERSIA, the country now called Iran, so 'one in 5 now' is a person from Iran; veterINARIan read backwards gives IRANI.
explanation.definitionFit: Irani is a word for a native or inhabitant of Iran, the modern state that was formerly Persia.

clue.text: Setting down two things musician might do for audience

indicators.note: an audience listens, so the words are judged by how they come across when spoken

parts.note: a musician might play and sing

explanation.surface: A performer puts down their instrument after doing two kinds of musical act for a crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For audience' sounds like performing for listeners, but it signals that the two verbs are run together and heard.
explanation.definitionFit: Placing something means putting it in position, the same act as setting it down somewhere.

clue.text: Best part of visual increased tenfold

indicators.note: multiplying by ten turns one Roman numeral into a bigger one, so a letter is swapped

parts.note: optical means relating to sight, visual

explanation.surface: The finest section of an image has been magnified ten times.
explanation.walkthrough: In OPTICAL, the Roman numeral C (100) is increased tenfold to M (1,000), giving OPTIMAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Optimal describes the most favourable or effective option available, which is the top or finest choice.

clue.text: Esme Llywellyn's a little malodorous

indicators.note: a little means only a small portion, so the answer is a slice of the longer phrase

parts.note: the letters run across the gap between the two names

explanation.surface: A woman named Esme Llywellyn is said to be slightly whiffy.
explanation.definitionFit: Malodorous is a formal word for giving off an unpleasant odour, which is what a stinky thing does.

clue.text: Sup tasty prepared remains

indicators.note: food that is prepared has been chopped and assembled, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to eat a delicious dish that has been made ready from leftovers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remains' looks like leftovers in a kitchen surface, but it is the verb meaning stays.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay put is to keep still in the same spot and not move, the verb sense of remaining.
